questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The opportunity for more practical application of theory especially within my chosen field. As some who wants to work in conservation I found that Australia possesses a higher degree of expertise.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The people at UTAS were extremely helpful and accommodating making the whole process very straightforward even before arrival. They were also quick to answer questions over email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were multiple introduction seminars and events specifically targeted at exchange and study abroad students which were very informative.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I used
flatmates.au
and got lucky by finding a fairly affordable place with some really friendly people. It was about 20-30 min from campus by bus which was fine in the morning but made getting home at night after studying late at the library a little challenging. If possible try to get something in the Sandy Bay area.
It was also a little stressful as we were getting quite close to the departure date before I got anything. This is not uncommon as many places will be looking for a flatmate that can move in fairly soon, so it’s hard to arrange anything too far ahead. I’d also advise looking in a bunch of different facebook groups for Hobart housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Depending on how far off campus you live getting home by public transport in the evening/night can be a pain. If you like being really social you might risk missing out on some of the events hosted by the uni accomodations.
The upside is that it is WAY cheaper than on campus housing. Do be aware that many of the houses are on the older side and not really insulated, meaning it can get pretty cold indoors in the winter, make sure to check the heating situation in the place your looking at.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You send a priority list to the echange coordinator and they have to do the registration for you. If you wanna change your courses you have to contact them again later either by email or (better) in person. It's pretty easy though.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UTAS website and the exhange coordinators (they were pretty easy to contact)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was fine, didn't get all my top priority courses since some of them ended up clashing and others got filled but that's how it goes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to research some backup courses incase you don't get the exct ones you had planned. You can always ask the exchange coordinators for recommendations.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Good level to the courses, matches what I found back home for the most part. Be aware that taking second year courses is an option, but might mean they have more expectations that you've had certain first year courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Depends on the course, but generally a lot of practical exercises including field and lab work in my case which was great this also included data collection and analysis for use in report writing. Be prepared that assignments are a big part of the assessment, depending on your courses you may not have any exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Antarctic Ecology
Biodiversity conservation
Fauna of Tasmania
Marine Resource Management and Conservation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Biodiversity conservation was great with some great opportunites for field excursions
Fauna of Tasmania gave a really good insight of both theory and how it could be applied
Antarctic ecology had an awsome teacher and offered great insight into scientific practice with some reall cool prac classes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I found meat to be fairly expensive. The visa was also quite expensive at around 8000 dkk, last I heard this might go up again in the coming years.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university gym is great. They offer a four month membership which is perfect.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Loads of clubs for basically all interests. They have a clubs and societies event where you get to meet  bunch of them. A lot of good opportunities if you like to be active or outdoors.

The student association (TUSA) also orgnised a bunch of trips you could sign up for.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I took my open water diver certificate which was awsome (though also kinda cold in winter) - I actually found it to be cheaper than at home which was surprising but great since Tassie offers some georgeous diving.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking, it is beautiful, wish I had gone out more. Also go on the public transport ferry, it is dirt cheap but a beutiful short ride, and you can explore around a new area for the day.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy, no real language barrier helps a lot. Very similar culture to Europe.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Most of them are really friendly. Obviously many already have esstblished friends, but just jump in and don't be afraid to approach people, especially in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There is some effort at acknowleding the traditional owners of the land which I really appreciated. otherwise just really enjoyed the outdoor culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
This will depend on what you are studying and what you are used to. Personally, as someone studying biology, I was not used to the amount and quality of assignments we had to do, as such i would advise:
1. Get an idea EARLY of the kind of assignments (e.g. how many words and references you need) and when they are do. Research takes time and will slow down writing, plan for this
2. Try to plan out you assignments, don't count on being able to finish all of them the week before they are do, they Will pile up.
3. Remember to have fun, don't spend all your time studying, grade are likely to be converted to pass/fail

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the TUSA food bank for cheap food.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I feel much stronger academically than before I went. I got a lot more opportunities to practise research and do data analysis than back home, not to mention all the practical work and awesome field excursions. 
Also meeting all the new people was great. Made some really solid friends and felt really welcome which was so nice.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Time management. I really underestimated the number of assignments and how much time they would take. I feel I spent way to much time at the library.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
